anomalies.observed: U2 (ATtiny45-20P) connects SCK to PB3 (pin 2) and POT to PB4 (pin 3) and has no TACH connection, while U3 (ATtiny13V-10S) connects SCK to PB2 (pin 7), POT to PB3 (pin 2) and TACH to PB4 (pin 3).
anomalies.expected: The two alternative ATtiny footprints should have identical pin assignments (SCK=PB2, POT=PB3, TACH=PB4) so the same firmware works with either build.

evidence.quote: U2 ATtiny45-20P: XTAL1/PB3 (pin 2) -> SCK, XTAL2/PB4 (pin 3) -> POT
U3 ATtiny13V-10S: PB2 (pin 7) -> SCK, PB3 (pin 2) -> POT, PB4 (pin 3) -> TACH

anomalies.impact: A board built with U2 cannot read the fan tachometer and uses different SCK/POT pins than a U3 build, so one firmware image cannot serve both options.

anomalies.observed: R3 pulls the RST net up to VCC and R6 pulls the TACH net up to VCC.
anomalies.expected: RST and TACH are 5V logic signals (the ATtiny runs from +5V), so their pull-ups should return to +5V, not to VCC, which is the input of the LM1117-5.0 and therefore higher than 5V.

evidence.quote: R3 10K: top -> VCC, bottom -> RST; R6 10K: top -> VCC, bottom -> TACH

anomalies.impact: RST and TACH would be pulled to the higher VCC rail, exceeding the ATtiny's absolute maximum ratings and potentially damaging the MCU or the fan tach input.

parsed.summary: The schematic contains two deviations: the two alternative ATtiny footprints (U2/U3) have inconsistent pin assignments, and the RST/TACH pull-ups (R3/R6) return to the unregulated VCC rail instead of the +5V logic rail.
